title: Ariane 5 Flight 501: inertial-reference software assumptions migrated from Ariane 4 into a new flight envelope
summary: The Ariane 5 maiden flight failed after both inertial-reference systems ceased providing valid guidance data. The Inquiry Board traced the technical pathway to an unprotected conversion overflow in software inherited from Ariane 4: an alignment function that was useful before liftoff and retained for commonality kept running during Ariane 5's much more aggressive early trajectory, producing a value outside a 16-bit signed-integer range. The record is promoted as an official-source-backed incident shell, with a mirror warning for the full report PDF.

type_payload.system: flight-control/guidance stack including redundant inertial reference systems, onboard computer, nozzle controls, and software reused from Ariane 4

sequence_of_events.event: Launcher behavior was nominal until roughly H0 + 36 seconds.
Backup and active inertial-reference systems ceased functioning due to the same software exception.
Diagnostic bit patterns from the failed active SRI were interpreted by the onboard computer as flight data.
The onboard computer commanded large nozzle deflections for an attitude deviation that had not actually occurred.
Aerodynamic loads led to breakup and self-destruction.

type_payload.proximate_cause: Guidance/control system acted on invalid inertial-reference data after both SRIs failed from the same unprotected conversion exception.
type_payload.root_cause_source_language: specification and design errors in the software of the inertial reference system
contributing_factors: Ariane 4 alignment software behavior was retained on Ariane 5 for commonality though it served no purpose after Ariane 5 liftoff.
The Ariane 5 trajectory generated horizontal-velocity-related values beyond assumptions made for Ariane 4.
The vulnerable alignment function was not tested under simulated Ariane 5 flight conditions.
The overall simulations used simulated SRI output rather than including the SRI or detailed SRI simulation.
latent_conditions: Common-mode failure in redundant systems that shared identical software and environmental assumptions.
Hidden assumptions in justification documents were not made explicit enough for external review.
Reuse carried prior flight-envelope assumptions into a new envelope without sufficient validation.
decisions_that_mattered: Retaining the post-liftoff alignment function for commonality.
Leaving specific conversions unprotected on the assumption that values would remain physically bounded.
Not including trajectory data/specification and realistic SRI behavior in tests and simulations.
recommendations_extracted: Switch off the SRI alignment function immediately after liftoff; more generally, run no software function during flight unless needed.
Use realistic input data and as much real equipment as technically feasible in complete closed-loop system testing.
Identify implicit assumptions in code and justification documents and check them against equipment restrictions.
Include trajectory data in specifications and test requirements.
counterfactuals_source_grounded: A closed-loop test including realistic Ariane 5 trajectory data and SRI behavior could have detected the failure pathway.
Disabling the alignment function after liftoff would have removed the unnecessary failure-producing computation.

links.note: Numeric range assumption and software-reuse assumption escaped their valid domain.
